1.
Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State, apprised the Court that he has received the instructions, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be finally disposed off.

2. Heard Sri Rishabh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I,
for the State.
3. The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in FIR/Case Crime No.137 of 2018, under Sections 419,420,467,468 and 504 IPC, Police Station Bansdeeh Road, District Ballia during pendency of the trial.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and others and according to the FIR,
applicant and other accused prepared forged sale deed of the father of the informant.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegations levelled against the applicant are totally false and considering the fact that a civil suit is also pending since the year 1970, the anticipatory bail application of co-accused Robin Singh, the brother of the applicant, has been allowed by this Court vide order dated 9.1.22024 passed in Criminal Misc.Anticipatory Bail Application No.8434 of 2023.He

sentences.text: next submits that the case of applicant is at par with him.

6. He further submits that present dispute is purely a civil dispute and after investigation charge sheet has also been filed even without arrest of the applicant and cognizance has been taken on 28.8.2024.
7.

He further submits that after submission of charge sheet custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary and applicant is having apprehension if he will appear before the court concerned then he will be sent to jail.
8. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history.

9. Per contra, learned AGA, however, opposed the prayerfor anticipatory bail but could not dispute the fact that in the present matter without arrest of the applicant charge sheet has been filed and cognizance has also been taken.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Considering the fact that prima facie present dispute appears to be civil dispute and without arrest of the applicant charge sheet has been filed and apprehension of arrest raised by applicant cannot be completely ruled out, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of the trial.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail anticipatory application is allowed.

13. In the event of arrest of the applicant-Ritesh Singh involved in the aforesaid case crime number,
shall be released on bail till the conclusion of the trial case on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Presiding Officer/Court concerned with the conditions:-
(i) that the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(ii) that the applicant shall not leave India without previous permission of the court;
(iii) that the applicant shall not temper with the evidence during the trial;

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.

15. It is made clear that the observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
